text:
sara: monitoring alerted on repeated retries and p99 east-west latency to svc/gpu-infer in us-west-2, looks like one pod is getting the bulk of traffic. anyone awake? :wave:

devops-bot: alert: svc/gpu-infer retries > 10% for last 5m, p99 latency 420ms (normal < 80ms)

matt: on it. which service exactly and kube-proxy mode?

sara: service is ClusterIP gpu-infer-prod, kube-proxy in ipvs mode (defaults). pods 6 across 3 nodes. Prom shows ~78% of connections hitting gpu-infer-5 on gpu-node-3. retries spike aligns with node kernel rollouts yesterday.

anton: could be ipvs hashing skew after kernel bump (we saw similar with multi-queue RDMA NICs). RDMA offload + ECMP changes can bias flows.

lee: can someone paste ipvs stats from node gpu-node-3?

sara: sure, grabbing from gpu-node-3 now:
```
# ipvsadm -L -n --stats
VIP: 10.100.2.10:8080 masq  ->  10.200.1.5:8080  Masq  0  0  78012
                                         ->  10.200.1.6:8080  Masq  0  0  2000
                                         ->  10.200.1.7:8080  Masq  0  0  1500
                                         ->  10.200.2.5:8080  Masq  0  0  1300
                                         ->  10.200.2.6:8080  Masq  0  0  1000
                                         ->  10.200.3.5:8080  Masq  0  0  900

# note: first backend (10.200.1.5) has ~78k pkts, others ~1-2k
```

jess: also see dmesg on that node with RDMA fallback messages around the same time: 
```
rdma_cm: rdma_sock: falling back to TCP, reason=0x3
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.1: RDMA: port 1: client failed to create qp, falling back
```

matt: that aligns. quick check: `ip link show` on gpu-node-3 shows an MTU mismatch on the ib0/interface used for pod traffic.

sara: pasted ip link snippet:
```
2: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000\3: ib0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000\```

anton: MTU mismatch between overlay and RDMA fabric + kernel ipvs hash can cause flows to concentrate due to ECMP/route heuristics. also kernel hash function changed in the rollout, so combination is unlucky.

lee: short mitigations: 1) restart kube-proxy on that node to rebuild ipvs tables (fast), 2) disable RDMA offload temporarily, or 3) roll back kernel if we confirm it's the change. conntrack entries might also be sticky.

jess: we can also check `conntrack -L | grep 10.200.1.5` — if a bunch of stale entries point to that pod, clearing them will rebalance new flows. but be careful with conntrack deletes during traffic peak.

matt: kube-proxy has a flag `--ipvs-scheduler` we could try setting to `lc` (leastconn) instead of default `rr` to help distribution, but that requires a rolling restart of kube-proxy on all nodes. temporary restart on the hotspot node first.

sara: draining gpu-node-3 would move pods but we can't afford that right now. please try kube-proxy restart and conntrack prune on that node only.

lee: running: `systemctl restart kube-proxy` on gpu-node-3 now. i'll also run `conntrack -D -d 10.200.1.5` to delete flows for that pod (only for IPv4).

matt: heads up, restarting kube-proxy will briefly rebuild ipvs rules -> expect a few seconds of extra retries but should rebalance afterwards.

(8m later)
matt: update: restarted kube-proxy and pruned conntrack on gpu-node-3. ipvs stats now more even: first backend down to ~6k pkts vs others 4–5k. retries dropped dramatically. p99 back to ~70ms.

sara: amazing, thanks. any next steps?

anton: we should schedule: 1) validate MTU across fabric and overlay, 2) add a canary kernel rollout for RDMA-enabled nodes, 3) consider adding a kube-proxy preflight that checks NIC offload/MTU alignment before kernel upgrades.

jess: logging a ticket to follow up on RDMA fallback behavior with the NIC vendor. add dmesg + ipvs dump.

sara: ok locking this thread. if retries climb again i'll reopen. thanks all. :tada:
